sentences.text: The petitioner was a collection agent in Reliable Cooperative Society Limited.
The said Society allegedly collected huge amounts from the investors with a promise to return the same with handsome rate of interest.

The complainant also deposited a sum of Date: 2023.05.19 Rs.43,25,000/ with the abovementioned Cooperative Society but 16:36:16 IST Reason:
nothing was returned to him.
This led to registration of FIR No.25/2019 under Sections 406, 420, 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 against the office bearers and employees of the Society including the petitioner.
3. The petitioner was arrested on 28082019 and is in custody for more than 3 years, 8 months or so.
4. The petitioner applied for his release on bail.
The High Court allowed the bail application on 18 012021 subject to depositing a sum of Rs.20,00,000/ along with a personal bond of Rs.1,00,000/ with one solvent surety.
5. The petitioner could not deposit the abovestated amount, hence, he moved an application for exemption to deposit the said amount.
The High Court vide impugned order dated 23012023 has allowed the petition in part and reduced the amount from Rs.20,00,000/ to Rs.10,00,000/.
The petitioner still being unable to pay Rs.10,00,000/ as a condition for his release on bail, he has approached this Court.
6. We have learned counsel for the parties and perused the counter affidavit filed on behalf of the State of Madhya Pradesh.
It is not in dispute that two office bearers of the Cooperative Society, who are the main accused have already been released on bail, subject to their depositing a sum of Rs.20,00,000/ each.
Both of them are stated to have complied with that condition.
The petitioner was admittedly working as collection agent of the Society.

It appears to us that the petitioner is not in a position to comply with the onerous condition of deposit of Rs.10,00,000/.
7.
Taking into consideration the period the petitioner has already spent in custody, we are satisfied that the condition imposed by the High Court while granting bail to him deserves to be set aside.
8. The deposit of Rs.10,00,000/ as a condition precedent for the petitioners release on bail as imposed by the High Court in the modified order, is thus set aside.
9. Let the petitioner be released on bail, subject to his complying with other terms and conditions imposed by the High Court.
10 The impugned order of the High Court is modified to the extent indicated above.
11. The Special Leave Petitions are disposed of in aboveterms.
(VISHAL ANAND) (PREETHI T.C.)
ASTT. REGISTRARcumPS COURT MASTER (NSH)
